content.title: About
content.content: Shortbread is a traditional Scottish biscuit made from butter, sugar, flour and sometimes a pinch of salt. It has a dense, crumbly texture and a delicate buttery flavor with a hint of sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shortbread originated in Scotland in the 18th century and was a favorite of the royal family.
It is traditionally cut into rectangular or round pieces, often dusted with powdered sugar.
The classic recipe uses only butter, with no leavening agents.
In the United States shortbread is often called “butter cookies” and used as a base for desserts such as cheesecakes.
Many variations exist, adding nuts, dried fruit, chocolate or spices.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates and fats provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and D
items.content: Butter supplies vitamins A and D, important for vision and bone health.

items.title: Provides calcium
items.content: Calcium supports healthy bones and teeth.

items.title: Small amount of iron
items.content: Iron contributes to oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Flour adds a modest amount of fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Butter may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Shortbread is rich in fats and sugars, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Flour contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shortbread can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with tea or coffee, used as a base for desserts, crumbled over ice cream, or sprinkled on cupcakes. It can also be gently warmed to enhance the buttery aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store shortbread in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator to prevent the butter from turning rancid. Discard if it develops a stale smell or off‑texture.
